intro: India's drug law. Punishment depends heavily on quantity — 'small', 'intermediate' or 'commercial' — as notified by the government for each drug. It also offers treatment instead of prosecution for people struggling with addiction.

sections.p: Each drug has a notified 'small quantity' and 'commercial quantity'. For example, for ganja (cannabis) small quantity is up to 1 kg and commercial is 20 kg or more; for heroin, small is up to 5 g and commercial is 250 g or more. Anything in between is 'intermediate'.
k: Bhang (cannabis leaves) isn't covered by the Act's definition of ganja — it is regulated by state excise laws

sections.p: Producing, manufacturing, possessing, selling, buying, transporting or using drugs illegally.
sections.pen: Small: up to 1 year and/or ₹10,000. Intermediate: up to 10 years + up to ₹1 lakh. Commercial: 10–20 years + ₹1–2 lakh
Up to 1 year and/or ₹20,000 for cocaine, morphine, heroin and similar; up to 6 months and/or ₹10,000 for other drugs

sections.p: Financing drug trafficking, or harbouring people involved in it.
Repeat offenders face one and a half times the punishment. For specified large quantities, repeat offenders may face death.

Officers searching without a warrant must record reasons. Before a personal search, you must be told you have the right to be searched in front of a Gazetted Officer or a Magistrate. Courts often acquit when these steps are skipped.
For commercial quantities, bail is granted only if the court is satisfied there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and won't offend on bail.

A person addicted to drugs who's charged with consumption or small-quantity possession and volunteers for de-addiction treatment at a recognised centre can be protected from prosecution. Courts can also release convicted addicts for treatment.
